baa_10y_spread.proxy_note: Moody's Baa corporate bond yield minus the 10Y Treasury -- a long-run investment-grade credit-risk-premium PROXY, not the literal ICE BofA IG OAS series this system quotes daily. Real history back to 1986. Useful for direction and episode timing (did credit broadly tighten/widen, and when); its magnitude runs tighter than IG OAS and far tighter than HY OAS, so never quote its level as if it were either.

history_digest.sentence: The 30-year Treasury yield (5.29%) first reached this level on Aug 17 and has been there on 31 of the 47 sessions since; before this run, the last time was Jun 2007, and only briefly (2 sessions); it was last there routinely until Feb 2002. This run's high was 5.67% on Oct 7, last matched in Jul 2001. Today's reading is at or above the reading on 81 of every 100 days of the last 30 years, but about average (46th percentile) since 1977. Every reading in the 1980s was at or above today's 5.29%.

history_digest.sentence: The 10-year TIPS real yield (2.76%, dated 10-21) first reached this level on Sep 23 and has been there on 19 of the 20 sessions since; before this run, the last time was Nov 2008 (during the 2007-09 Global Financial Crisis). This run's high was 2.95% on Oct 5, last matched in Nov 2008. Today's reading is at or above the reading on 99.2 of every 100 days since 2003. But TIPS only exist since 2003: the Cleveland Fed's model real rate, back to 1982, puts real rates at the 80th percentile of the last 30 years and the 54th since 1982 — high against the last 30 years, about average since 1982.

history_digest.sentence: The 2-year Treasury yield is up 118bp this year — the 9th-largest rise through this date in 50 years (bigger: 2022 +376bp, 1994 +255bp, 1981 +250bp, …). Over the last 12 months it is up 1.20 points; a 12-month rise at least that big has started 8 times since 1977. Measured from each start, the S&P 500 (price only) was lower a year later in 3 of 8 (any 12-month stretch since 1962: 24.4%), and a recession began within two years in 2 of 8 (any two-year stretch since 1962 outside a recession: 27.4%).
